key_insight: A neural spline flow learns a smooth, invertible geometry map so finite element PDEs can be solved on a fixed reference mesh while preserving the pullback weak form.
engineering_relevance: This reduces mesh-generation bottlenecks for complex CAD-like domains and enables reusable, structured FEM workflows with conventional discretization machinery.
method: Use monotone rational-quadratic spline coupling layers to guarantee a strictly positive Jacobian determinant.
Train a shared NSF conditioned on low-dimensional latent geometry codes in an auto-decoder setup.
Predict codes for unseen shapes with an encoder, then solve the pulled-back PDE on the reference domain.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical benchmarks showing that sufficiently accurate learned mappings produce reliable FEM solutions and that the framework remains exactly equivalent to solving on the learned domain.
watch_item: Overall accuracy still depends on geometric fidelity, so mapping error can limit solution quality even if the FEM solve itself is stable.
paper_title: Neural Spline Flow Diffeomorphisms for Pullback Finite Element Methods on Complex Domains
